name: yourproject-model
notes: The child's OWN asset model — its catalog kinds as config, never code (ADR-0007). Two kinds show the whole grammar: a governed kind with a lifecycle and a record-only kind that refs it. Create a store governed by this model and drive it with the same CLI as any other: python -m dskit.assets init --store ./yourproject_store --model configs/asset-model.json. Governance is exactly as strong as this file's hash — the store pins it at init, so changing what the model permits is a new, visible identity. Rename the kinds to YOUR domain's nouns; the engine checks structure and ref topology only, so meaning lives in these notes.

dataset.notes: The governed kind: a lifecycle means records move draft -> published -> retired by explicit transition, and any move not listed below is refused (default-deny). Right for the things the child MANAGES — config is governed, evidence is immutable.

name.notes: The human alias every kind must declare (ADR-0009) — versions of the same dataset share it.

description.notes: What this dataset is for. Free text; the engine checks structure only.

settings.notes: The dataset's knobs. Hash-material: change a setting, get a new version_id — same content, same identity.

artifact.notes: The record-only kind: no lifecycle block, so records are registered once and never transitioned — right for EVIDENCE (outputs, plots, snapshots) that is what it is. The required ref means an artifact can never float free: the referenced version_id must already be in the store, and must be a dataset.

digest.notes: sha256 of the artifact's bytes — anchor identity on content, keep the path as provenance.
